question: An item costs 30 yuan to purchase, and 100 units are sold per day when the selling price is 40 yuan. For every 1 yuan increase in the selling price, 5 fewer units are sold per day (the price increase must be an integer number of yuan). Find the maximum daily profit. (Unit: yuan)
solution: Let the price increase be \(x\) yuan. The profit is \(P=(10+x)(100-5x)=-5x^2+50x+1000=-5(x-5)^2+1125\). The maximum is 1125 when \(x=5\).

solutionMethods.explanation:
Because the price increase must be a whole number of yuan, compare profits at consecutive allowed increases. Let \(k\) be the increase in yuan. Nonnegative sales give \(k=0,1,\ldots,20\), and daily profit is \(P(k)=(10+k)(100-5k)\).

For \(k=0,1,\ldots,19\),
\[
P(k+1)-P(k)=(11+k)(95-5k)-(10+k)(100-5k)=45-10k.
\]
This difference is positive for \(k=0,\ldots,4\) and negative for \(k=5,\ldots,19\). These comparisons cover every consecutive pair of feasible increases, so profit rises up to \(k=5\) and then falls. At \(k=5\), the margin is \(15\) yuan and sales are \(75\) units. The maximum daily profit is therefore \(15\times75=1125\) yuan.
solutionMethods.label: Compare consecutive integer increases

reference.question: An item costs 30 yuan to purchase, and 100 units are sold per day when the selling price is 40 yuan. For every 1 yuan increase in the selling price, 5 fewer units are sold per day (the price increase must be an integer number of yuan). Find the maximum daily profit. (Unit: yuan)
reference.solution:
Method 1: Complete the profit square

Let the price increase be \(x\) yuan. The profit is \(P=(10+x)(100-5x)=-5x^2+50x+1000=-5(x-5)^2+1125\). The maximum is 1125 when \(x=5\).

Method 2: Compare consecutive integer increases

Because the price increase must be a whole number of yuan, compare profits at consecutive allowed increases. Let \(k\) be the increase in yuan. Nonnegative sales give \(k=0,1,\ldots,20\), and daily profit is \(P(k)=(10+k)(100-5k)\).

For \(k=0,1,\ldots,19\),
\[
P(k+1)-P(k)=(11+k)(95-5k)-(10+k)(100-5k)=45-10k.
\]
This difference is positive for \(k=0,\ldots,4\) and negative for \(k=5,\ldots,19\). These comparisons cover every consecutive pair of feasible increases, so profit rises up to \(k=5\) and then falls. At \(k=5\), the margin is \(15\) yuan and sales are \(75\) units. The maximum daily profit is therefore \(15\times75=1125\) yuan.
